## Resolved local blockers
### B1 — final canonical integration suite: resolved locally
Each failure was triaged rather than broadly skipped. Firmware fixes cover
signer/session revocation, display binding, Solana field disclosure, excluded
certified/LUT policy, setup lifecycle, chain wire guards and nested-confirm
unwinding. Canonical tests were corrected where their fixtures encoded an
impossible Solana ATA shape, the wrong XRPL MemoData field, or abandoned a
valid maximum-amount confirmation. The final Compose harness also executes the
five owned power-cycle storage tests instead of silently skipping them. Final
regular result: **755 passed, 75 deliberate skips, zero failures**.
### B2 — screenshot evidence certification: resolved locally
The original script tolerated pytest failure and gated only on a nonzero PNG
count. That behavior has been removed while retaining screenshots and JUnit
for diagnosis.
The screenshot phase now fails on pytest failure and the report generator
cross-checks captured sequences against its JUnit result. Final result:
sequences; every declared screen captured**.
### B3 — partial-release capability gates: resolved locally
All slices report firmware `7.15.0`, while capabilities differ across partial
trees. A test gated only on `>= 7.15.0` can demand a later capability from an
earlier slice. Do not solve this with a release-specific python-keepkey branch
The canonical harness reads `KK_RELEASE_MISSING_CAPABILITIES` only for partial
slice CI and retains version gates only where the behavior is genuinely
versioned. Stack 00b declares its pre-existing safe-reset, THOR deposit,
maximum-amount, legacy-router and protected-Ping gaps plus the later unknown-
token, entropy, Osmosis, Ripple, Hive, prompt-unwind and session capabilities.
Stacks 01-04 retain the maximum-amount and later gaps; stacks 05-06 also mark
the not-yet-landed ERC-7730 runtime review; stacks 07-09 retain both EVM review
gaps. Stack 10 removes the EVM gaps; stack 12 also removes Hive. The
`storage-v19-kdf` and `solana-lut-attestation` controls remain explicitly absent
through stack 12 and become mandatory at stack 13. Stack 13 declares no missing
capabilities. No
release-only python-keepkey fork is used. Ten final policy-convergence unit
tests are likewise compiled only in stack 13: the assertions describe behavior
that does not exist in earlier partial trees, and all remain active in the
release candidate rather than being skipped or weakened there.
### B4 — ARM-only compile and stack-reslice regressions: resolved locally
ARM compilation exposed duplicate declarations/scratch state, an unused
contract-confirmation parameter, and a shadowed Maya memo-loop index that host
tests did not reject. Each correction was applied at its earliest owning slice
and propagated forward. The regular ARM build retains 17,316 bytes of SRAM
reserve (16,384-byte floor); bitcoin-only retains 38,220 bytes.
Reconstructing the corrected 14-slice topology also caught a substantive TRON
regression in the superseded candidate: message display had been truncated and
the typed-hash blind-signing AdvancedMode fence had been lost. The authoritative
tree preserves full-byte `confirm_bytes()` review and requires AdvancedMode for
typed-hash signing. This is why the older green emulator tree is not a release
candidate.
The final workflow audit also removed the non-release `zcash-privacy` CI and
publication leg, made the regular emulator leg exercise the shipped Zcash-
enabled multi-coin product, repaired its publication artifact selection,
added the missing ARM matrix labels, and removed a duplicate `strategy` key
that made `release.yml` structurally invalid. Every workflow passes `actionlint`.
Topic-branch pushes no longer duplicate the same expensive workflow; each
stacked PR base is explicitly included in the `pull_request` trigger, so the
single run validates GitHub's synthetic merge for that adjacent slice.
The intermediate-slice audit also restored the full/bitcoin-only product
defines in stacks 01-04, scoped Hive and Zcash privacy dispatch out of
bitcoin-only, removed duplicate Zcash layout/handler declarations, retained
the checked RNG-health API, moved response-buffer right-sizing to stack 03,
linked the Orchard and constant-time Pallas sources when first required,
versioned the slice-01 RedPallas tests with the pinned crypto API, scoped Zcash
and TRON test suites out of reduced builds, and removed a temporary Zcash
signing-contract regression from stacks 09-10.
The pinned clang-format-20 gate and zero-warning cppcheck gate also pass; the
last cppcheck finding was a duplicated EIP-1559 fee-bound condition removed at
its owning stack. Partial handler bodies at stacks 03-12 retain the mutable
protobuf dispatcher ABI with narrow inline cppcheck suppressions; exact
cppcheck 2.20 runs pass at both stack 03 and stack 12, and the suppressions are
absent from the complete stack-13 source tree.
### B5 — skipped power-cycle storage gates: resolved locally
The ordinary python-keepkey image did not contain a restartable emulator binary,
so U1-U4 in the release report skipped even while the aggregate integration job
passed. Running them manually exposed two stale canonical assumptions: an
unframed V17 record was forced through a CRC-only helper, and the test still
expected 7.15 to erase a newer normal-band record despite the intentional
`SUS_TooNew` non-destructive bridge.
The canonical test now derives the declared wipe-or-refuse policy from the

the regular full-suite skip count fell from 80 to 75.

historical_added_lines_absent_now: # Refresh auto-lock only for accepted workflow progress
A stalled signing session remained unlocked indefinitely while a host polled
GetFeatures: the firmware RX wrapper reset idle time before validating any USB
frame. Remove that wrapper and renew the deadline only at accepted workflow
stages that request another message. This covers Bitcoin, Ethereum, Binance,
Cosmos/Tendermint, Osmosis, THORChain, MAYAChain, and EOS streams. Accepted
recovery edits and reset entropy preserve the setup ceremony deadline too.
EOS chunks carrying zero bytes while data remains, empty recovery backspaces,
unrelated polls, and incomplete frames do not count as progress. Empty recovery
characters are rejected instead of matching the cipher's terminating NUL.
Progress can renew a deadline at home because some signing handlers wait there;
it cannot wake a completed screensaver lock.
Native USB-callback regressions reproduce the old GetFeatures/incomplete-frame
bypass and verify real Bitcoin, Ethereum, EOS, and recovery progress across
multiple idle periods, followed by lock when progress stalls. Invalid Bitcoin
ACKs still terminate signing. The tests exercise completed protocol stages;
individual fragments of a very slow message do not extend its deadline.
On-device confirmation remains unchanged. Host-driven `layoutHomeForced()` and
`leave_home()` transitions no longer renew the timer; only validated workflow
progress or physical button activity does.

historical_added_lines_absent_now: 7.15 is the non-destructive V17 bridge. It preserves unreadable newer
normal-band storage across a downgrade by returning `SUS_TooNew`, clearing only
the RAM shadow, and refusing every commit until the user explicitly wipes. This
is not a parser compatibility shim: the older firmware never loads the newer
record. Reinstalling the newer firmware can therefore recover the wallet.
The retained contract is upgrade preservation, contiguous shipped-version
recognition, explicit refusal of formats the running firmware cannot parse, and
byte-identical preservation while that refusal is active. Bitcoin-only storage
uses the parallel `SUS_BitcoinOnlyLocked` path. The canonical python-keepkey
reboot tests derive which policy a firmware tree implements so older releases
that deliberately reset unknown storage and 7.15's non-destructive bridge can
share one branch without version-string gates.
Signed physical upgrade verification remains a final release gate; emulator
tests prove firmware storage behavior but cannot prove bootloader signature
